9-panel cinematic storyboard CONTACT SHEET derived from Image 1. Mix Wide, Medium, and Tight shots of the same scene.

Layout: a rigid 3x3 grid of 9 equal rectangular cells in a 16:9 landscape image. Each cell is exactly 1/3 of the width and 1/3 of the height. Separate cells with a thin black gutter.
- Content must not cross, bleed, or overlap a gutter. No collage.
- Each cell is a complete, independently framed shot — not a crop of a larger scene.

Scene: medium wide, eye level, Scarlett (Image 2) has slid into the booth with Mina (Image 3); the open coral lipstick rests between them beside fries and two paper cups, Scarlett (Image 2) and Mina (Image 3) sit opposite each other in the red booth, fries and paper cups between them, rain-streaked window forming a warm reflective backdrop, INT. NEIGHBORHOOD DINER — AFTERNOON, neighborhood_diner (Image 5), Warm late-afternoon light pours through the rain-streaked window, creating soft highlights and reflections while the interior remains cozy and gently contrasted., Red vinyl, warm amber and honey light, dark window gray, green utility jacket, black clothing, cream paper, and coral., Scarlett (Image 2), Mina (Image 3), Server (Image 4), Modern social-first product photography with tactile, editorial energy. Products shown in real-life context -- hands opening packaging, fingers pressing textures, products on bathroom shelves, kitchen counters, rumpled linen. Close-up detail shots emphasize material and finish. Flat-lays with curated minimal arrangements. Color-matched backgrounds that complement the product. Every frame feels like something you would screenshot and save

Every panel is a shot of the same scene as Image 1 — keep the characters, wardrobe, lighting, color grade, and texture consistent across all panels.

No text, dialogue bubbles, scene numbers, or watermarks.

Reference images define identity — keep every referenced character, object, and location consistent with its reference image; never render a reference image itself as a separate panel or subject.
Image 1 (primary): Primary source scene — generate 9 variant shots from this image
